If the overhead to translate a rival solution into the owner's vocabulary consistently exceeds the latency of the owner generating a weaker native solution, the system is operating efficiently; if T_O is low but rival solutions are still rejected, it is suppressing.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the system lacks a mechanism to attempt translation (T_O is never measured), this metric cannot be computed.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If T_O is high but the resulting translated solution is vastly more robust than L_owner's native solution, rejecting it based on T_O > S_L may still constitute suppression of quality in favor of speed.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If L_owner's vocabulary lacks the expressive power to host the translated cross-cutting solution, T_O is effectively infinite, which masks suppression as a technical impossibility.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"For each problem, measure the cost T_O of mapping L_rival's valid cross-cutting solution onto L_owner's vocabulary. Then measure S_L, the time L_owner takes to produce its own valid solution. If T_O < S_L and the system still fails to adopt the cross-cutting solution, this is a positive instance of suppression. Count the frequency of this event. Efficiency is indicated when T_O > S_L, justifying the rejection of the rival solution on computational grounds.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
